locator: VIII, lect. 9 n. 1041: cannot itself cause motion without a principal mover moving it
interpretation: In the descending form of the argument, 'what a mover uses as an instrument in causing motion cannot itself cause motion without a principal mover moving it, as a stick cannot cause motion independently of the hand'; Aquinas adds that this holds in an ordered array of mobiles as in instruments, 'because not every one would consider the second mover an instrument of the first'. Read as the same proposition as SCG I.13 [15], with Aquinas' own remark extending it from instruments to every ordered second mover. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
